question: Section 335 of the BNS defines—
explanation: s.335 defines when a person is said to make a false document or false electronic record; forgery is defined in s.336(1).

question: Under Explanation 1 to s.335, a man's signature of his own name—
options: Is forgery only on a will
Is forgery only if made abroad
explanation: Expl. 1 to s.335: 'A man's signature of his own name may amount to forgery.'

question: B, authorised by A to fill in a signed cheque up to ₹10,000, fraudulently fills in ₹20,000. B has committed—
explanation: Illustration (d) to s.335: B commits forgery by filling up the cheque beyond his authority.

question: Basic forgery under s.336(2) is punishable with—
options: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: s.336(2): imprisonment of either description up to two years, or fine, or both.

question: Forgery intending the forged document to be used for cheating (s.336(3)) is punishable with—
explanation: s.336(3): imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine (formerly s.468 IPC).

question: Which document is expressly NEWLY mentioned in Section 337 (forgery of public records)?
explanation: s.337 now includes 'an identity document issued by Government including voter identity card or Aadhaar Card'.

question: Forgery of a will is punishable under s.338 with—
options: Imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years, and fine
explanation: s.338 (valuable security, will, etc.): imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine.

question: Forgery of a valuable security under s.338 is cognizable only when—
options: The valuable security is a promissory note of the Central Government
It is committed by a public servant
explanation: BNSS First Schedule: s.338 is non-cognizable, except when the valuable security is a Central Government promissory note.

question: A person who uses a forged document as genuine, knowing it to be forged, is punished under s.340(2)—
options: In the same manner as if he had forged it
Only if he forged it himself
explanation: s.340(2): 'shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document or electronic record'.

question: Possessing a forged Aadhaar card, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine, is punishable under s.339 with up to—
explanation: s.339: for a document described in s.337 (which includes Aadhaar), up to seven years and fine.

question: Merely possessing a seal knowing it to be counterfeit (without further intent) is punishable under—
explanation: s.341(3): whoever possesses any seal, plate or other instrument knowing it to be counterfeit — up to three years and fine.

question: Fraudulently destroying a will to cause injury to a beneficiary is an offence under—
explanation: s.343: fraudulently cancelling, destroying, defacing or secreting a will, authority to adopt or valuable security — life or up to 7 years, and fine.

question: Falsification of accounts (s.344) can be committed by—
options: A clerk, officer or servant (or person acting as such) in respect of the employer's records
explanation: s.344 applies to a clerk, officer or servant, or a person employed or acting in that capacity.

question: Under the Explanation to s.344, a charge of falsification of accounts—
options: May allege a general intent to defraud without naming a person, sum or date
explanation: Explanation to s.344: it is sufficient to allege a general intent to defraud.

question: A 'property mark' under s.345(1) is a mark denoting that—
options: Goods are manufactured by a company
Movable property belongs to a particular person
Goods are of a certain quality
explanation: s.345(1): a mark used for denoting that movable property belongs to a particular person is called a property mark.

question: Under s.345(3), a person using a false property mark escapes punishment if—
options: The prosecution fails to prove loss
He proves that he acted without intent to defraud
explanation: s.345(3): punishable 'unless he proves that he acted without intent to defraud' — the burden is on the accused.

question: Counterfeiting a mark used by a public servant to denote the quality of property (s.347(2)) is punishable with up to—
explanation: s.347(2): up to three years, and fine; counterfeiting another person's property mark (s.347(1)) is up to two years.

question: Which of these Chapter XVIII offences is compoundable?
options: s.349 — selling goods with a counterfeit property mark
explanation: BNSS s.359(1): ss.345(3), 347(1) and 349 are compoundable by the person to whom loss or injury is caused.

question: Falsely labelling a carton so that customs officers believe it contains goods different from its real contents is an offence under—
explanation: s.350(1): making a false mark on a receptacle to cause a public servant or any person to believe it contains different goods — up to 3 years.

question: The IPC offences on currency-notes and bank-notes (ss.489A-489E) are now found in—
explanation: The BNS moved currency and bank-note offences to Chapter X (coin, currency-notes, bank-notes and Government stamps).
